classification.difficultyReason: Construct an unsignposted symbolic proof by transferring q across parallel lines, expressing a triangle angle using r+s, and combining angles on a straight line.

spec.description: Unshaded geometry preserving A–B–C, G–F–E and F–C–D collinearity, BF and DE segments, both matching parallel arrows, all point labels and four angle sectors. Ordinary source grey strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: ABC is parallel to GFE; q=angle FBC, p=angle BFC, r=angle FED and s=angle FDE. Coordinates encode these exact incidence and parallel relationships without supplying numerical measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and labels appear; the proof and derived angle BFG are answer content.

answer.short: $\angle BFG=q$ and $\angle DFE=180^{\circ}-(r+s)$. Angles on the straight line $GFE$ give $q+p+180^{\circ}-(r+s)=180^{\circ}$, hence $p+q=r+s$.
answer.worked:
Since $ABC\parallel GFE$, alternate angles are equal:
$$\angle BFG=q.$$
The angles in triangle $DFE$ sum to $180^{\circ}$:
$$\angle DFE=180^{\circ}-(r+s).$$
Angles on the straight line $GFE$ sum to $180^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BFG+\angle BFD+\angle DFE&=180^{\circ}\\q+p+180^{\circ}-(r+s)&=180^{\circ}\\p+q&=r+s.\end{align*}$$
